subject: DeltaWorks SDK compatibility & gating: request for stability commitments
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@deltaworks.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DeltaWorks: SDK compatibility and feature-gating ask

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Quick intro — I'm Alex (Head of Integrations at DeltaWorks). We're planning to adopt Redwood's hosted API + SDK in our orchestration product later this quarter. Before we start integrating at scale, a couple of asks from our engineering and product teams: 

- Can Redwood commit to a clear deprecation timeline for any breaking changes to the streaming generation API and the client SDK (JavaScript + Python)?
- We're particularly worried about the streaming token schema change announced informally last month; we need to know whether that will be surfaced as a major semver bump for SDKs or handled behind a feature flag.
- We'd like a compatibility matrix that maps current v1 behaviors to the proposed v2 behaviors so we can plan migration tests.

I've attached a simple compatibility matrix that shows the areas we care about (streaming payload, chunk delimiting, authorization header changes). Could we get a short sync this week to align on a mutual action plan + gating approach?

Proposed times: Wed 11/4 10–11am PT or Thu 11/5 9–10am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Alex Ramos
Head of Integrations, DeltaWorks
alex.ramos@deltaworks.ai
Attachment: deltaworks_sdk_matrix.xlsx
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@deltaworks.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DeltaWorks: SDK compatibility and feature-gating ask

Alex — thanks for the clear matrix. Happy to take this on.

Quick response / next steps from our side: 
- I'll loop in product (Marissa) and engineering (Jonas) to produce a short compatibility note and propose gating options.
- We can do Wed 11/4 10am PT — that works for me; if that suits you I'll send a calendar invite.

Internal notes for Marissa / Jonas:
- DeltaWorks explicitly calls out streaming payload schema and auth header changes as blockers for their Canary customers. They want either:
  * a feature-flag rollout that preserves v1 behavior for a set time, or
  * a non-breaking shim in our SDKs that normalizes the two schemas client-side.
- Risk/opportunity: if we provide a short-term shim in mainline SDKs, we reduce churn for ISVs but add maintenance burden for N months.

Attachments I'm dropping here: rdw_compatibility_notes.pdf (initial ask capture) and a short proposed MAP outline (proposed-map.md).

Ben Carter
Senior Partnerships, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: rdw_compatibility_notes.pdf
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@deltaworks.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DeltaWorks: SDK compatibility and feature-gating ask

Alex / Ben — thanks for surfacing this and for the matrix. I've sketched a recommended approach below that balances stability for partners with our ability to iterate: 

Recommended policy (product):
- Short-term: implement a feature-flag-controlled streaming schema toggle. Default for hosted API: v2, but request header X-RDW-Schema: v1 will enable legacy behavior for 90 days after rollout.
- SDK strategy: publish SDK adapters that translate v1 client calls into v2 server formats for both JS and Python. Maintain the adapter in the main SDK repo for 6 months, then move it to a separate compatibility package if long-term needed.
- Enterprise (Dedicated/Private): offer a 12-month extended compatibility window on request (contractual).
- Deprecation notice cadence: 60-day RFC -> 90-day sunset after GA of the new schema for hosted. For enterprise, sunset subject to contractual terms.

Open engineering questions for Jonas:
- Can the runtime support header-based routing without an infra-wide rollout?
- Any KV-cache / tokenization side effects we should call out?

If this is acceptable, I'll draft a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to share with DeltaWorks on Wednesday's call. I've uploaded a short playbook and the draft MAP to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_MAP 

Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Integrations
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: feature-flag-playbook.pdf
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@deltaworks.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DeltaWorks: SDK compatibility and feature-gating ask

Marissa / team / Alex — quick technical confirmation from runtime: 

- Header-based routing: feasible. We can respect X-RDW-Schema headers at the gateway and route to a compatibility codepath. We'll need a small canary rollout (edge region) to validate before global flip.
- SDK adapter approach: engineering can deliver lightweight adapters for JS/Python that perform the translation at the client layer (normalize chunk framing + auth header mapping). Initial target: 6-week delivery for the adapter + tests. We'll maintain the adapter in the monorepo for 6 months and then propose moving to redwood-compat-* packages.
- KV cache impact: legacy v1 streaming appended bytes to the KV stream differently — this is a material difference for long-context workloads. Our adapter will include a translation layer that maps v1 framing to v2 KV delta writes, but there will be a performance delta (~2–4% CPU overhead on inference nodes during translation). We should surface that to DeltaWorks so they can decide whether to accept slight latency/cost increase or run their migration in a dedicated capacity pool.

Action items:
1) Ben: confirm Wed 11/4 10am PT invite + list of DeltaWorks attendees.
2) Marissa: draft MAP and include the 90-day hosted sunset + 12-month enterprise option. 
3) Alex / DeltaWorks: sign off on proposed short-term adapter plan and indicate whether you want Redwood to host the adapter package long-term or the DeltaWorks team will own it after 6 months.

I'll also create an internal RFC for the feature-flag rollout and loop in runtime infra for a canary. Happy to review the MAP on the call.

Jonas Weber
Engineering Lead, Runtime
jonas_weber@redwood.com
